page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding 8.0 GB of memory per core. A key hardware feature is the inclusion of 1919 GB of local SSD storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a moderate to weak processing profile. The server scored in the bottom 25% for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large-block uncached reads and writes, though cached small-block reads remain in the bottom 25%. Redis SET operations and small model LLM inference achieved average tier results, while larger model processing and compression tasks fell into the lower percentiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server provides high local storage density and dedicated memory resources, making it a viable option for workloads requiring significant local disk space without demanding top-tier CPU compute. The hardware configuration is best suited for local database hosting, caching layers, and storage-intensive applications that benefit from the bundled 1919 GB SSD and 64 GB memory capacity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.2xlarge is an x86_64 server configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, 64.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 1919 GB local SSD. Running on the KVM hypervisor, it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark results indicate modest CPU capabilities, with stress-ng and Geekbench scores placing it in the bottom 25% for compute performance. However, it maintains average performance in uncached memory bandwidth and Redis SET operations. Given its high local storage capacity and 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for storage-heavy deployments. It is best suited for databases, caching systems, and general-purpose workloads requiring substantial local SSD capacity.
